label: Left rite
summary: The rite (a regional form of a faith) shown as the left-hand icon of a notification.
details: A notification (the short message that pops up for the player) can show an icon on each side of its text. Vanilla passes this rite to the rite icon in the left icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window, and shows that icon only when there is a valid rite. The game documents no return type.

label: Left tenet
summary: The tenet (a core belief of a faith) shown as the left-hand icon of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to the tenet icon in the left icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type; going by the icon it feeds, it is a tenet.

label: Left title
summary: The title (a barony, county, duchy, kingdom or empire) shown as the left-hand icon of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to the coat of arms in the left icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Right artifact
summary: The artifact shown as the right-hand icon of a notification.
details: Vanilla shows it in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window, and the artifact messages name it in their text ("You acquired …", with the left artifact as the second one). The game documents no return type.

label: Right character
summary: The character whose portrait is shown on the right-hand side of a notification.
details: Vanilla shows a shoulders-up portrait of this character in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window, only when there is a valid character. The game documents no return type.

label: Right doctrine
summary: The doctrine (one of a faith's rules or stances) shown as the right-hand icon of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to the doctrine icon in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Right dynasty
summary: The dynasty whose coat of arms is shown on the right-hand side of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to a dynasty coat of arms in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Right faith
summary: The faith whose icon is shown on the right-hand side of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to the faith icon in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Right house
summary: The house (a branch of a dynasty) whose coat of arms is shown on the right-hand side of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to the house coat of arms in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Right rite
summary: The rite (a regional form of a faith) shown as the right-hand icon of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to the rite icon in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Right tenet
summary: The tenet (a core belief of a faith) shown as the right-hand icon of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to the tenet icon in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Right title
summary: The title whose coat of arms is shown on the right-hand side of a notification.
details: Vanilla passes it to a title coat of arms in the right icon slot of notification pop-ups and the message window. The game documents no return type.

label: Notification heading
summary: The heading text of a notification.
details: Vanilla prints it as the large heading line at the top of notification pop-ups. Here "title" means the text heading, not a landed title.

label: Notification tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a notification.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the notification templates and the message window, and in one place as a line of text itself.

label: Notification type
summary: The type of a notification, which says what kind of message it is.
details: Vanilla checks the type's flags to pick a layout: tournament rewards (flag `tournament_reward`) and finished contracts (flag `contract_completion_reward`) get their own pop-ups, and messages whose type has no flags use the default one. The game documents no return type.

label: Has left icon
summary: Yes or no: whether the notification has an icon on its left-hand side.
details: Vanilla shows the left icon slot only when this is yes, and puts an empty spacer of the same size there when it is no.

label: Has right icon
summary: Yes or no: whether the notification has an icon on its right-hand side.
details: Vanilla shows the right icon slot (portrait, coat of arms, faith icon and so on) only when this is yes, and a spacer otherwise.

label: Contract succeeded
summary: Yes or no: whether the contract (a task taken on for pay) this notification reports on was completed successfully.
details: Vanilla uses it in the contract result pop-up to play a success animation when yes and a failure animation when no.

label: Has no icons
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the notification has no icon on either side.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it checks HasLeftIcon and HasRightIcon instead.

label: Has one icon
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the notification has exactly one icon.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it checks HasLeftIcon and HasRightIcon instead.

label: Notification itself
summary: A function on a notification that hands back the notification itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. In game texts Self follows other things, for example Character.Self passed as an argument; those lines belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Has two icons
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the notification has an icon on both sides.
details: Vanilla never uses it; it checks HasLeftIcon and HasRightIcon instead.

label: Access player value itself
summary: A function on a player value (the data behind a resource shown in the interface, such as merit) that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, it gives access to the player value itself. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf, which passes a widget along, is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Balance
summary: The balance of a player value, a decimal number shown next to the resource in the top bar.
details: Vanilla prints it with one decimal and switches to the negative text style when it is below zero, so it can be negative. Going by its name and this display, it is the regular gain or loss of the resource, not the amount held (that is GetValue).

label: Balance breakdown
summary: The data object behind a player value's balance, which vanilla hands to the lines that show where the gain or loss comes from.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data for the total line in the resource tooltip (whose own tooltip is a value breakdown) and for the merit balance breakdown text. The game documents no return type; the reading as a breakdown rests on those uses.

label: Balance total text
summary: The text of the total line in a resource's tooltip, the summed-up balance.
details: Vanilla uses it as the label text of the total line in the resource tooltip (the game text TOTAL_BREAKDOWN_LABEL is just this function).

label: Value name
summary: The name of the resource a player value stands for (vanilla shows merit through this type).
details: Vanilla uses it in the heading of the resource tooltip, written as name, a colon, and the current amount from GetValue.

label: Current level
summary: A whole number: going by its name, the number of the level the player has reached in this value.
details: Vanilla's resource tooltip shows levels (merit ranks are one example). Vanilla never names this function on this type; the lines that use GetCurrentLevel belong to court grandeur and are only a hint.

label: Current level name
summary: The name of the level the player has reached in this value.
details: Vanilla shows it in the resource tooltip next to the level label (see GetLevelConcept).

label: Level label
summary: The name of the levels of this value, used as a label before the current level's name.
details: Vanilla writes it with a colon in front of the current level's name in the resource tooltip.

label: Maximum level text
summary: The text that shows the highest level the given character can reach in this value.
details: Vanilla shows it only when HasNonStandardLevel is yes for the same character, for example as the merit cap next to a character's total merit, with GetMaxLevelBreakdown as its tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose maximum is shown.

label: Maximum level breakdown
summary: The text that explains where the given character's maximum level in this value comes from.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltip of the maximum level, for example under the heading "Maximum merit level".

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose maximum is explained.

label: Maximum level number
summary: A whole number: the position of the highest level the given character can reach in this value.
details: Vanilla compares it with the segments of the merit bar and darkens every segment above it, so levels out of reach look greyed out.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose maximum is used.

label: Next level name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the next level the player can reach in this value.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Progress tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the progress bar toward the next level of this value.
details: Vanilla shows it when the mouse is over the progress bar in the resource tooltip.

label: Progress to next level
summary: A decimal number: how far the player has come toward the next level of this value.
details: Vanilla uses it as the fill of the progress bar in the resource tooltip.

label: Progress label
summary: The label text above the progress bar toward the next level of this value.
details: Vanilla shows it in the resource tooltip, only when there is a next level (HasNextLevel).

label: Current amount
summary: A whole number: the amount of this resource the player has now.
details: Vanilla shows it in the heading of the resource tooltip after the resource's name.

label: Has next level
summary: Yes or no: whether this value has a level above the current one.
details: Vanilla shows the progress label and bar in the resource tooltip only when this is yes, so they disappear at the top level.

label: Has non-standard level
summary: Yes or no: whether the given character has a maximum level in this value that differs from the usual one.
details: Vanilla shows the maximum level text (GetMaxLevel) only when this is yes, for example the merit cap. The "differs from the usual" reading rests on the name and that use.

label: Reset update frame
summary: An action with no result: going by its name, it resets the record of when this value was last updated.
details: Vanilla calls it when the mouse enters a resource tooltip, which suggests it makes the tooltip's numbers refresh; that rests on the name and this use.

label: Player value itself
summary: A function on a player value that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Lines with Self on other types, such as Character.Self, are only a hint.

label: Access plot line itself
summary: A function on a plot line (going by its name, a line drawn in a graph of the interface) that hands back the object itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Smooth point index at mouse
summary: A decimal number: going by its name, the position along a graph line nearest the mouse, including the part between two points.
details: Vanilla never uses it. Compare GetSnappedIndexNearMouse, which by its name gives the nearest whole point.

label: Smooth value at mouse
summary: A pair of numbers (x and y): going by its name, the spot on a graph line nearest the mouse, worked out between its points.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Plot area
summary: A rectangle: going by its name, the area a graph line is drawn in.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Point index at mouse
summary: A whole number: going by its name, the number of the graph point nearest the mouse.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Point value at mouse
summary: A pair of numbers (x and y): going by its name, the graph point nearest the mouse.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Has point near mouse
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether there is a point of the graph line near the mouse.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Plot line itself
summary: A function on a plot line that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Lines with Self on other types are only a hint.

label: Access 3D portrait view itself
summary: A function on a 3D portrait view (going by its name, an interface element that shows a portrait in 3D) that hands back the object itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Animation tooltip
summary: A text about the animation the portrait editor's 3D view plays.
details: The 3D view window of the engine's portrait editor shows it as the tooltip of its portrait, but only while ShouldShowAnimationInfo is true; otherwise the tooltip stays empty. Going by its name it describes the animation; the game documents nothing more.

label: Portrait data
summary: The portrait data the portrait editor's 3D view draws.
details: The 3D view window of the engine's portrait editor hands it to its portrait widget as that widget's portrait context. The game documents no return type.

label: Portrait model
summary: The 3D model (entity) the portrait editor's 3D view draws, picked by a number.
details: The 3D view window of the engine's portrait editor uses it with the number 0 as its portrait widget's entity. What other numbers pick is not documented, and the game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A number picking the entity; vanilla passes 0.

label: Save portrait screenshot
summary: Saves a screenshot of the portrait editor's 3D view; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the 3D view's Save Screenshot button in the engine's portrait editor. Where the file goes is not documented.

label: 3D portrait view itself
summary: A function on a 3D portrait view that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Lines with Self on other types are only a hint.

label: Access portrait data itself
summary: A function on portrait data (going by its name, the information behind one portrait) that hands back the object itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Portrait data name
summary: A text: going by its name, the name of this portrait data.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetName on other types (traits, activity types) gives their display names and is only a hint.

label: Portrait data itself
summary: A function on portrait data that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Lines with Self on other types are only a hint.

label: Access editor animation itself
summary: A function on an animation entry of the portrait editor that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by the type's name, it is one animation in the portrait editor's list. Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Editor animation name
summary: A text: going by its name, the name of an animation in the portrait editor's list.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetName on other types is only a hint.

label: Editor animation itself
summary: A function on an animation entry of the portrait editor that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Lines with Self on other types are only a hint.

label: Access portrait editor itself
summary: A function on the portrait editor window that hands back the object itself.
details: The portrait editor is an engine window for character portraits that vanilla's own interface files never use; going by its functions (reloading assets, opening files), it looks like a work tool for editing portraits. PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint.

label: Can optimize textures
summary: Whether the portrait editor can run its texture optimization (yes or no).
details: The engine's portrait editor shows its Run Texture Optimization button only when this is true. When it is true is not documented.

label: Shown portrait types
summary: The portrait types the portrait editor shows as previews.
details: The engine's portrait editor fills a grid with it, one tile per portrait type: each tile shows the type's key and a portrait image, and a click opens it in the 3D view. Going by the name, these are the portrait types active in the chosen portrait type group. The game documents no return type.

label: Portrait age
summary: The age setting of the portrait editor as a whole number.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as "Age: ...%" above its age slider, so it is the slider's position as a percent rather than an age in years.

label: Age slider position
summary: The portrait editor's age setting as a decimal number from 0 to 1.
details: The engine's portrait editor uses it as the value of its age slider, which runs from 0 to 1; moving the slider calls OnAgeChanged. GetAge shows the same setting as a percent.

label: Animations
summary: Going by its name, the list of animations the portrait editor offers.
details: Vanilla never uses it; each entry is presumably a portrait editor animation entry, which the input does not confirm.

label: Animation tooltip
summary: A text about the animation of one portrait type's preview in the portrait editor.
details: The engine's portrait editor adds it to each preview tile's tooltip ("Click to open 3D view ..."), passing that tile's portrait type, but only while ShouldShowAnimationInfo is true. Going by its name it describes the animation; the game documents nothing more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The portrait type whose preview the tooltip is for.

label: Camera name
summary: A text: going by its name, the name of the camera (view angle) the portrait editor uses.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; CameraItem.GetCameraName in the royal court screenshot window is a different type and only a hint.

label: Child generator
summary: The portrait editor's child generator; going by its name, a tool that makes a child's look from parents.
details: Vanilla never uses it. Its return type is ChildGenerator.

label: Animation file
summary: A text describing the file the portrait editor's current animation comes from.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as the tooltip of the open-file button next to its animation list; the button opens that file with OpenCurrentAnimationFile.

label: Camera file
summary: A text describing the file the portrait editor's current camera (view angle) comes from.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as the tooltip of the open-file button next to its camera list; the button opens that file with OpenCurrentCameraFile.

label: Environment file
summary: A text describing the file the portrait editor's current environment (lighting and background) comes from.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as the tooltip of the open-file button next to its environment list; the button opens that file with OpenCurrentEnvironmentFile. The game's portrait environments live in gfx/portraits/environments.

label: Ethnicity file
summary: A text describing the file the portrait editor's current ethnicity (a set of looks for a people) comes from.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as the tooltip of the open-file button next to its ethnicity list; the button opens that file with OpenCurrentEthnicityFile.

label: Gene accessory text
summary: A text about the accessory the gene selected in the portrait editor uses.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it in a text box only when the selected gene is an accessory gene (clothes, hair, headgear and similar). What the text lists is not documented.

label: Gene file
summary: A text describing the file the gene selected in the portrait editor (one part of a character's looks) is defined in.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as the tooltip of the open-file button next to its gene list; the button opens that file with OpenCurrentGeneFile.

label: Portrait type file
summary: A text describing the file the portrait editor's current portrait type group is defined in.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as the tooltip of the open-file button next to its portrait type group list; the button opens that file with OpenCurrentPortraitTypeGroupFile. Vanilla's one portrait type group, human, is in common/portrait_types.

label: DNA text
summary: The DNA string (the coded description of a character's looks) of the portrait being edited.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it in the tooltip of its Copy DNA String button ("DNA String: ..."); that button copies it with OnCopyDNA.

label: Environment name
summary: A text: going by its name, the name of the environment (lighting and background) the portrait editor uses.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Portrait data
summary: The portrait data of the portrait being edited.
details: Its return type is PortraitDataContext, the data behind one portrait. The engine's portrait editor sets it as the data of its standard preview portraits, such as the full-body one that opens the 3D view when pressed.

label: Portrait image
summary: The portrait image (texture) the portrait editor shows for one portrait type.
details: The engine's portrait editor uses it as the picture of each preview tile, passing the tile's portrait type. The game documents no return type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The portrait type to draw the portrait for.

label: Selected animation
summary: A pair of whole numbers: going by its name, the position of the selected animation in the portrait editor.
details: Vanilla never uses it, and the input does not say what the two numbers stand for.

label: Selected gene
summary: The gene (one trait of a character's look) selected in the portrait editor.
details: Its return type is GeneItem. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Gene color X
summary: A decimal number: the X coordinate of the selected color gene's color.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as "X: ..." under Color Coordinates, only for color genes (skin, eye or hair color). Going by the name, X and Y together pick the color from the gene's color palette; the game does not say so.

label: Gene color Y
summary: A decimal number: the Y coordinate of the selected color gene's color.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as "Y: ..." under Color Coordinates, next to the X coordinate from GetSelectedGeneTemplateColorX, only for color genes.

label: Gene strength
summary: A decimal number: how strongly the selected gene's template is applied.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as "Strength: ..." for every gene except color genes.

label: Slider maximum
summary: A decimal number: the highest value of the portrait editor's attribute sliders.
details: The engine's portrait editor uses it as the upper end of each slider in its attribute slider list; GetSliderMinValue gives the lower end.

label: Slider minimum
summary: A decimal number: the lowest value of the portrait editor's attribute sliders.
details: The engine's portrait editor uses it as the lower end of each slider in its attribute slider list; GetSliderMaxValue gives the upper end.

label: Has sliders
summary: Whether the portrait editor has any sliders to show (yes or no).
details: When it is true, the editor shows its slider list and enables the Reset All button; when it is false, it shows "No sliders available" instead.

label: Has sub-genes
summary: Whether the gene selected in the portrait editor has sub-entries (gene items) to choose from (yes or no).
details: The engine's portrait editor shows the gene item's name on its entries only when this is true. OnChangeSubGeneItemLeft and Right step through those entries.

label: Is current tab
summary: Whether the given tab is the one open in the portrait editor (yes or no).
details: The engine's portrait editor shows each tab's content only while this is true for it. SetContentTab opens a tab.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the tab to check.
fields.values: a tab name in quotes; vanilla uses 'editor_tab', 'preview_tab1' and 'preview_tab2'

label: Is accessory gene
summary: Whether the gene selected in the portrait editor is an accessory gene (clothes, hair, headgear and similar) (yes or no).
details: When it is true, the editor shows a Sub Group header and the gene's accessory text from GetCurrentGeneAccessoryString.

label: Is color gene
summary: Whether the gene selected in the portrait editor is a color gene (skin, eye or hair color) (yes or no).
details: When it is true, the editor shows the color's X and Y coordinates; when it is false, it shows the gene's strength and the buttons that step through the gene's entries instead.

label: Is morph gene
summary: Whether the gene selected in the portrait editor is a morph gene (one that changes the shape of something) (yes or no).
details: When it is true, the editor shows a Gene template header for the gene.

label: Is slider mode
summary: Whether the portrait editor's sliders are in the given mode (yes or no).
details: The editor's Slider mode checkboxes (None, Genes, Attributes) show which mode is on with it; SetSliderMode switches the mode.

label: Is slider portrait type
summary: Whether the portrait editor's sliders are set to use the given portrait type (yes or no).
details: The editor shows one checkbox per portrait type after "Using:" and marks the chosen one with it; SetSliderPortraitType changes the choice.

label: Age changed
summary: Applies a change of the portrait editor's age slider; it returns nothing.
details: The engine's portrait editor calls it whenever the age slider's value changes. It takes no argument, so the new value comes from the slider.

label: Previous animation
summary: Steps back to the previous animation in the portrait editor's animation list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the left arrow button beside the Animations list.

label: Next animation
summary: Steps on to the next animation in the portrait editor's animation list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the right arrow button beside the Animations list.

label: Previous gene
summary: Steps back to the previous gene in the portrait editor's gene list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the left arrow button beside the Gene list.

label: Next gene
summary: Steps on to the next gene in the portrait editor's gene list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the right arrow button beside the Gene list.

label: Previous gene entry
summary: Steps back to the previous entry of the selected gene in the portrait editor; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of a left arrow button that the editor shows for every gene except color genes.

label: Next gene entry
summary: Steps on to the next entry of the selected gene in the portrait editor; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the right arrow button that pairs with OnChangeSubGeneItemLeft.

label: Copy DNA
summary: Copies the DNA string (the coded description of the looks) of the portrait being edited; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Copy DNA String button, whose tooltip shows the string from GetDNA. OnPasteDNA is its counterpart.

label: Copy persistent DNA
summary: Copies the scripted-character DNA of one portrait type's preview to the clipboard; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the Copy Persistent DNA button on each preview tile of the portrait editor. The button's tooltip says this form breaks less easily than the DNA string and is the one to use for historical characters. OnPastePersistentPortraitInfo is its counterpart.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The portrait type whose preview is copied.

label: Cycle ethnicity
summary: Switches the portrait editor to another ethnicity (a set of looks for a people) in its list; it returns nothing.
details: The left and right arrow buttons beside the Ethnicity list call it with -1 and 1, so the number is the step through the list.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How far to step through the list: -1 for the previous ethnicity, 1 for the next.

label: Cycle portrait type group
summary: Switches the portrait editor to another portrait type group in its list; it returns nothing.
details: The left and right arrow buttons beside the Portrait Type Group list call it with -1 and 1. Vanilla has a single group, human.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How far to step through the list: -1 for the previous group, 1 for the next.

label: Randomize DNA
summary: Makes new random DNA for the portrait from the chosen ethnicity; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Randomize DNA button under the ethnicity choice. OnGenerateFromEthnicityExcept does the same but keeps the template.

label: Randomize except template
summary: Makes new random DNA for the portrait from the chosen ethnicity, except for the template; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's "Randomize except template" button. Which template is kept (going by the editor, most likely the selected gene's) is not documented.

label: Next camera
summary: Switches the portrait editor to the next camera (view angle) in its list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the right arrow button beside the Camera list.

label: Next environment
summary: Switches the portrait editor to the next environment (lighting and background) in its list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the right arrow button beside the Environment list.

label: Paste DNA
summary: Applies a copied DNA string to the portrait being edited; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Paste DNA String button. OnCopyDNA is its counterpart.

label: Paste persistent DNA
summary: Applies copied scripted-character DNA to the portrait being edited; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Paste Persistent DNA button. OnCopyPersistentPortraitInfo is its counterpart.

label: Previous camera
summary: Switches the portrait editor back to the previous camera (view angle) in its list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the left arrow button beside the Camera list.

label: Previous environment
summary: Switches the portrait editor back to the previous environment in its list; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the left arrow button beside the Environment list.

label: Randomize portrait ID
summary: Gives the portrait being edited a new random portrait ID; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Randomize Portrait ID button. What the ID changes in the look is not documented.

label: Reload assets
summary: Loads the portrait assets (such as models and textures) again; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Reload Assets button, so changed files can be seen without restarting.

label: Reload color palettes
summary: Loads the color palettes (the images skin, eye and hair colors are picked from) again; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Reload Color Palettes button. Vanilla's palettes are images in gfx/portraits.

label: Reload decals
summary: Loads the decal textures (images laid over a portrait's skin) again; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Reload Decal Textures button.

label: Reset DNA to neutral
summary: Resets the DNA of the portrait being edited to neutral values; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's "Reset DNA to neutral" button.

label: Restart portrait
summary: Starts the portrait being edited over; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the portrait editor's Restart Portrait button. What exactly restarts (for example its animation) is not documented.

label: Optimize textures
summary: Runs the portrait editor's texture optimization; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the Run Texture Optimization button, which is shown only when CanOptimize is true. What the optimization does is not documented.

label: Open 3D view
summary: Opens the 3D view of the portrait editor for one portrait type; it returns nothing.
details: A preview tile calls it with its own portrait type, both when the tile is clicked and from its 3D View button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The portrait type to show in 3D.

label: Open animation file
summary: Opens the file the portrait editor's current animation comes from; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the open-file button beside the Animations list; the button's tooltip names the file (GetCurrentAnimationFileDesc).

label: Open camera file
summary: Opens the file the portrait editor's current camera comes from; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the open-file button beside the Camera list; the button's tooltip names the file (GetCurrentCameraFileDesc).

label: Open environment file
summary: Opens the file the portrait editor's current environment comes from; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the open-file button beside the Environment list; the button's tooltip names the file (GetCurrentEnvironmentFileDesc).

label: Open ethnicity file
summary: Opens the file the portrait editor's current ethnicity comes from; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the open-file button beside the Ethnicity list; the button's tooltip names the file (GetCurrentEthnicityFileDesc).

label: Open gene file
summary: Opens the file the gene selected in the portrait editor is defined in; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the open-file button beside the Gene list; the button's tooltip names the file (GetCurrentGeneFileDesc).

label: Open portrait type file
summary: Opens the file the portrait editor's current portrait type group is defined in; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the open-file button beside the Portrait Type Group list; the button's tooltip names the file (GetCurrentPortraitTypeGroupFileDesc).

label: Reset sliders
summary: Puts all of the portrait editor's sliders back to their starting values; it returns nothing.
details: It is the action of the Reset All button above the slider list, which is enabled only when HasAnySliders is true.

label: Portrait editor itself
summary: A function on the portrait editor window that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Lines with Self on other types are only a hint.

label: Open tab
summary: Opens the given tab of the portrait editor; it returns nothing.
details: The editor's tab buttons call it: Editor opens 'editor_tab', Compare 'preview_tab1', Compare 2 'preview_tab2' and Children 'children_tab'. IsCurrentContentTab checks which one is open.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the tab to open.
fields.values: a tab name in quotes, such as 'editor_tab'

label: Select animation
summary: An action with no result: going by its name, it makes an animation the selected one in the portrait editor.
details: Vanilla never uses it. It takes no argument, so which animation it selects is not clear from the input.

label: Set slider mode
summary: Switches the portrait editor's sliders to the given mode; it returns nothing.
details: The editor's Slider mode checkboxes call it with 'none', 'genes' or 'attributes'. IsSliderMode checks the mode.

label: Set slider portrait type
summary: Sets which portrait type the portrait editor's sliders use; it returns nothing.
details: The editor lists every portrait type with a checkbox after "Using:", and clicking one calls this with that type. IsSliderPortraitType checks the choice.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The portrait type the sliders should use.

label: Access portrait tooltip itself
summary: A function on a portrait tooltip (going by its name, the tooltip shown over a character portrait) that hands back the object itself.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is a different type and only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Portrait tooltip itself
summary: A function on a portrait tooltip that hands back the object itself; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Lines with Self on other types are only a hint.

label: Access portrait type itself
summary: A function on a portrait type that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, a portrait type is one of the body setups in common/portrait_types, such as male, female, boy and girl inside vanilla's human group. Vanilla never names this function on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is only a hint.

label: Portrait type group
summary: Going by its name, the group a portrait type belongs to, such as human; the game documents no return type.
details: In common/portrait_types the types male, female, boy and girl sit inside the group human. Vanilla never names this function on this type; the lines with GetGroup belong to doctrines and are only a hint.

label: Portrait type number
summary: A whole number: going by its name, the position of the portrait type in the game's list of them.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetIndex on other types is only a hint.

label: Portrait type key
summary: The script key of the portrait type (such as `male`), as text.
details: The engine's portrait editor shows it as the label of each preview tile and beside each checkbox of its slider portrait type choice.

label: Is portrait type valid
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the portrait type exists and can be used.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type. Elsewhere IsValid follows other things, for example a character's government, to test that it is there; that is only a hint.

label: Portrait type text
summary: A text: going by its name, a localized (translated) text for the portrait type, picked by its one argument.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type, and the argument is not documented. Localize on other types is only a hint.

label: Portrait type itself
summary: The portrait type itself, to pass on to another function.
details: The engine's portrait editor passes it from each preview tile to functions that need a portrait type, such as GetPortraitTexture, Open3dView and GetAnimationTooltip. The game documents no return type.

label: Access portrait type group itself
summary: A function on a portrait type group that hands back the object itself.
details: Going by its name, a portrait type group is a top-level entry of common/portrait_types, such as vanilla's human, holding its colors and its portrait types. Vanilla never names this function on this type; PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf is only a hint.

label: Portrait type group number
summary: A whole number: going by its name, the position of the portrait type group in the game's list of them.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetIndex on other types is only a hint.

label: Portrait type group key
summary: A text: going by its name, the script key of the portrait type group (such as `human`).
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; GetKey on other types is only a hint.

label: Portrait type
summary: Going by its name, a portrait type of this group; the game documents no return type.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type, and it takes no argument, so which of the group's types it gives is not clear. The lines with GetType belong to other types and are only a hint.

label: Is portrait type group valid
summary: Yes or no: going by its name, whether the portrait type group exists and can be used.
details: Vanilla never names it on this type; IsValid on other types is only a hint.
